plants.name: Snake Plant
plants.description: A tough, low-maintenance plant that tolerates low light and irregular watering, making it a great choice for beginners.

careGuide.watering: Water only when the soil is completely dry, roughly every 2–3 weeks.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed with a diluted liquid fertilizer once every 1–2 months during spring and summer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2–3 years, or once the roots outgrow the pot.
careGuide.cleaning: Wipe leaves with a damp cloth every few weeks to remove dust.

plants.name: ZZ Plant
plants.description: A glossy, drought-tolerant plant that thrives on neglect, perfect for busy students and low-light rooms.

careGuide.watering: Water only when the soil is fully dry, roughly every 2–3 weeks.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed sparingly, about once every 2 months during the growing season.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2–3 years, as growth is slow.
careGuide.cleaning: Dust leaves occasionally with a soft cloth.

plants.name: Money Plant (Pothos)
plants.description: A fast-growing trailing vine that adapts well to most indoor spaces and is very forgiving for new plant owners.

careGuide.watering: Water when the top inch of soil feels dry, about once a week.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed monthly with a balanced liquid fertilizer during the growing season.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 1–2 years or when roots fill the pot.
careGuide.cleaning: Rinse leaves under water occasionally to keep them dust-free.

plants.name: Spider Plant
plants.description: A resilient plant known for its arching leaves and small offshoot 'babies', ideal for hanging baskets or shelves.

careGuide.watering: Water when the topsoil dries out, about once a week.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed lightly once a month during spring and summer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 1–2 years as it grows quickly.
careGuide.cleaning: Trim brown leaf tips and dust leaves occasionally.

plants.name: Peace Lily
plants.description: An elegant flowering plant that thrives in shady spots and signals when it needs water by drooping slightly.

careGuide.watering: Keep soil consistently moist; water when the top inch feels dry, roughly twice a week.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed every 6–8 weeks with a balanced liquid fertilizer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot once a year or when it becomes root-bound.
careGuide.cleaning: Wipe leaves gently to keep them glossy and dust-free.

plants.name: Rubber Plant
plants.description: A bold plant with large, glossy leaves that makes a striking statement piece in any room.

careGuide.watering: Water when the top inch of soil feels dry, about once a week.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed monthly during the growing season with a balanced fertilizer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 1–2 years to support its growth.
careGuide.cleaning: Wipe large leaves regularly to keep them shiny and dust-free.

plants.name: Monstera Deliciosa
plants.description: A dramatic tropical climber with large, split leaves that becomes a focal point but needs room to spread.

careGuide.watering: Water when the top 2–3 inches of soil are dry, about every 1–2 weeks.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed monthly with a balanced liquid fertilizer during spring and summer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2 years, or when roots circle the pot.
careGuide.cleaning: Wipe the large leaves regularly to remove dust.

plants.name: Heartleaf Philodendron
plants.description: A graceful trailing vine with heart-shaped leaves that grows well in shaded rooms and forgives occasional neglect.

careGuide.watering: Water when the top inch of soil feels dry, about every 1–2 weeks.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed monthly with a balanced liquid fertilizer during the growing season.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 1–2 years or when roots fill the pot.
careGuide.cleaning: Wipe leaves with a damp cloth to keep them clean and glossy.

plants.name: Chinese Evergreen (Aglaonema)
plants.description: A durable foliage plant with patterned leaves that tolerates shade and indoor conditions well.

careGuide.watering: Water when the top 1–2 inches of soil are dry, about every 1–2 weeks.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed every 2 months with a diluted balanced fertilizer in spring and summer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2–3 years, as growth is slow.
careGuide.cleaning: Wipe leaves occasionally to remove dust.

plants.name: Lucky Bamboo
plants.description: A symbolic, low-maintenance plant often grown in water or moist soil, popular for desks and small spaces.

careGuide.watering: If grown in water, change it every 1–2 weeks and keep the roots submerged.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed lightly every 2 months with a diluted liquid fertilizer.
careGuide.repotting: Change its container only when it outgrows its current space.
careGuide.cleaning: Rinse stalks and leaves occasionally with clean water.

plants.name: Boston Fern
plants.description: A lush, feathery fern that loves humid air and constant moisture, best for people willing to give it regular attention.

careGuide.watering: Keep soil evenly moist and never let it dry out; water about twice a week.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed monthly with a diluted liquid fertilizer during spring and summer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot once a year or when roots fill the pot.
careGuide.cleaning: Trim brown fronds and mist or rinse the foliage to keep it fresh.

plants.name: Areca Palm
plants.description: A graceful, feathery palm that adds a tropical feel and helps soften larger indoor spaces.

careGuide.watering: Water when the top inch of soil is dry, keeping soil lightly moist.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed monthly during spring and summer with a balanced fertilizer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2 years or when roots become crowded.
careGuide.cleaning: Mist or wipe the fronds occasionally to prevent dust buildup.

plants.name: Parlor Palm
plants.description: A compact, slow-growing palm that tolerates shade and suits shelves, corners and small to medium rooms.

careGuide.watering: Water when the top inch of soil is dry, about every 1–2 weeks.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed every 2 months with a diluted balanced fertilizer in spring and summer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2–3 years, as growth is slow.
careGuide.cleaning: Wipe fronds gently with a damp cloth to remove dust.

plants.name: Aloe Vera
plants.description: A hardy succulent that stores water in its leaves, making it drought-tolerant and easy to care for.

careGuide.watering: Water deeply but infrequently; let the soil dry out completely between waterings.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed once or twice a year with a cactus/succulent fertilizer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2 years or when it outgrows its container.
careGuide.cleaning: Wipe leaves occasionally; avoid overwatering to prevent rot.

plants.name: Golden Barrel Cactus
plants.description: A slow-growing, spiny round cactus that needs very bright light and almost no watering, best for sunny windowsills.

careGuide.watering: Water only when the soil is completely dry, about every 3–4 weeks in summer and rarely in winter.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed once or twice during the growing season with a cactus fertilizer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 3–4 years using thick gloves or folded newspaper to handle the spines.
careGuide.cleaning: Dust gently with a soft brush; avoid wetting the crown.

plants.name: Christmas Cactus
plants.description: A trailing jungle cactus that blooms in cooler months and prefers moderate light and moisture unlike desert cacti.

careGuide.watering: Water when the top inch of soil is dry, about every 1–2 weeks; reduce slightly after flowering.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed monthly with a balanced fertilizer from spring to early autumn.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2–3 years, preferably after flowering.
careGuide.cleaning: Gently wipe the flat stem segments to remove dust.

plants.name: Zebra Haworthia
plants.description: A tiny striped succulent that tolerates indoor light better than most succulents and suits desks and shelves.

careGuide.watering: Water every 2–3 weeks once the soil is completely dry; water less in winter.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed once or twice during spring and summer with a diluted succulent fertilizer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2–3 years or when offsets crowd the pot.
careGuide.cleaning: Remove dead lower leaves and dust the rosette with a soft brush.

plants.name: Moon Cactus
plants.description: A small grafted cactus with a bright coloured top, popular as a desk plant but sensitive to overwatering and low light.

careGuide.watering: Water sparingly, about every 2–3 weeks, only when the soil is completely dry.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed once a month in spring and summer with a diluted cactus fertilizer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2 years in a small pot with fast-draining cactus mix.
careGuide.cleaning: Dust gently with a soft brush and avoid wetting the coloured top.

plants.name: Bunny Ears Cactus
plants.description: A pad-shaped cactus covered in soft-looking dots that need strong light and very little water to stay healthy.

careGuide.watering: Water only when the soil is fully dry, about every 2–3 weeks in summer and rarely in winter.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed once or twice during the growing season with a cactus fertilizer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 2–3 years using thick gloves or tongs, as the fine bristles irritate skin.
careGuide.cleaning: Dust with a soft brush; avoid touching the bristles.

plants.name: Echeveria
plants.description: A compact rosette succulent that needs very bright light to keep its shape and colour, ideal for sunny windowsills.

careGuide.watering: Water every 2 weeks once the soil is dry, keeping water out of the rosette centre.
careGuide.fertilizer: Feed once or twice during spring and summer with a diluted succulent fertilizer.
careGuide.repotting: Repot every 1–2 years in fast-draining cactus mix.
careGuide.cleaning: Remove dead lower leaves and dust gently with a soft brush.
